title: The universe is expanding – the Quran said it first
preview: Centuries before Hubble, the Quran described the heavens as expanding. Science caught up in the 20th century.
content:
# The Quran and the expanding universe

*"And the heaven We constructed with strength, and indeed, We are [its] expander."* — **Quran 51:47**

When this verse was revealed over 1,400 years ago, telescopes didn't exist. The idea that space itself could be stretching was unknown to science.

In the 1920s, Edwin Hubble observed that galaxies are moving away from each other. Today we call it the expanding universe. The Quran didn't just hint at it – it stated it plainly.

---

A book that invites you to reflect on the heavens and the earth – and science keeps finding reasons to be amazed.

title: Honey: a healing from your Lord
preview: The Quran called honey a cure for people. Modern science keeps proving it right.
content:
# Honey in the Quran

*"There emerges from their bellies a drink, varying in colors, in which there is healing for people. Indeed in that is a sign for a people who give thought."* — **Quran 16:69**

Allah points us to the bee and its honey as a sign and a healing. Today we know honey has antibacterial properties, helps wounds heal, soothes throats, and may support immunity.

The Quran didn't say "honey is nice" – it said there is **healing** in it and invited people to **think**. That combination of faith and reflection is at the heart of Islamic tradition.

---

Every time science uncovers another benefit of honey, it's another reminder of that verse.

title: Two seas that do not mix
preview: The Quran describes a barrier between salt and fresh water. Oceanographers found it in the real world.
content:
# Where two seas meet

*"He released the two seas, meeting [side by side]; between them is a barrier [so] neither of them transgresses."* — **Quran 55:19–20**

Where the Gulf meets the ocean, or where a river pours into the sea, you don't get one uniform mix. There's a visible boundary – different color, temperature, and salinity. The Quran called this over 1,400 years ago.

No boats or submarines existed to explore such places. Yet the verse speaks of two bodies of water that meet but are kept distinct. It's a sign for those who reflect.

---

Next time you see a river meeting the sea, remember: the Quran already told you they don't simply merge.

title: The first word revealed was "Read"
preview: Islam's first divine command wasn't pray or fight – it was to read, in the name of the One who taught by the pen.
content:
# Read – the first command

When the Angel Jibril (Gabriel) came to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) in the cave of Hira, the first word of the Quran revealed was:

**"Read."**

*"Read in the name of your Lord who created – created man from a clot. Read, and your Lord is the most generous, who taught by the pen, taught man that which he knew not."* — **Quran 96:1–5**

In a time when few could read, the faith that would preserve knowledge and build libraries started with a command to read and to honor the pen. That choice still defines Islam's relationship with learning.

---

Every book, every school, every search for knowledge echoes that first word: **Read.**

title: The Black Stone: touched by millions, unchanged
preview: Pilgrims have kissed and touched the Black Stone for over 1,400 years. It has never been replaced – and it never grew.
content:
# The Black Stone of the Kaaba

The Black Stone is set in a corner of the Kaaba in Makkah. During Hajj and Umrah, millions of people seek to touch or kiss it, following the practice of the Prophet (peace be upon him).

What's striking isn't only its place in ritual – it's the fact that after countless hands and lips, through centuries, the Stone is still there. It wasn't replaced. It didn't "grow" in size through retellings. It remains a single, tangible link to the earliest days of Islam.

The Prophet said the Stone was sent down from Paradise and was whiter than milk – it was the sins of people that turned it black. Touching it is an act of humility and love, not worship of the stone itself.

---

A stone that connects billions of believers to one House and one Lord.

title: Every deed is written – even a smile
preview: The Prophet said even a smile in the face of your brother is charity. Angels record it all.
content:
# Your smile is sadaqah

The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: *"Your smile in the face of your brother is charity."* (Tirmidhi)

Islam teaches that two angels sit with each person: one records good deeds, the other wrongs. But it goes further – the Prophet made clear that **good** includes the smallest acts: a smile, removing harm from the path, a kind word, or even greeting someone with peace.

That means every time you ease someone's day or lift their mood, it's not "just" kindness – it's an act that counts in the sight of Allah. You don't need wealth to build a record of good. You need intention and small, consistent mercy.

---

Amazing thought: your smile today could be written among your best deeds.
